validated_results.title: Meat and dairy consumption and subsequent risk of prostate cancer in a US cohort study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort reporting dairy food intake and incident prostate cancer risk with a target-specific hazard ratio.

extraction.population: Men aged 35+ years participating in the CLUE II study

sample_size.excerpt: In 1989, 3,892 men 35+ years old, who participated in CLUE II study of Washington County, MD, completed an abbreviated Block food frequency questionnaire.

cases.excerpt: Incident prostate cancer cases (n = 199) were ascertained through October 2004.

effect_size.excerpt: There was no association across tertiles of dairy or calcium with total prostate cancer, although compared tp < or =1 servings/week consumption of 5+ servings/week of dairy foods was associated with an increased risk of prostate cancer (HR = 1.65, 98% CI 1.02-2.66).

confidence_interval.excerpt: < or =1 servings/week: HR = 2.24; 95% CI 0.90-5.59) prostate cancer.
